solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: In Peru, let hero, ostensibly, reign

indicators.note: 'In' says the letters sit inside the run of words that follows, spanning their boundaries

blocks.note: the letters run unbroken across the end of Peru, all of let and hero, and the start of ostensibly

explanation.surface: A would-be dictator in Peru is apparently set to take power.
explanation.walkthrough: The commas break up the hidden run; ignore them and read straight through.
explanation.definitionFit: To dominate a group and be the one in charge is an idiomatic way to say to hold sway or govern.

clue.text: Artist and doctor: old, aggressive male

blocks.note: RA is a Royal Academician, the usual crossword artist
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification
O is the standard abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A painter and a physician, both elderly, described as a combative man.
explanation.walkthrough: The name comes from the violent action-film hero, used generically for a macho, belligerent man.
explanation.definitionFit: The film character's name has become a byword for a violently macho tough guy, so it is used as a common noun.

clue.text: Exponent of record with a beat you can hear

indicators.note: what you can hear is the sound of a word rather than its spelling, so a word spelt otherwise is wanted

blocks.note: a log is a written record, as a ship's log
taken as written
a beat in music is its regular pulse

explanation.surface: Someone who champions a recording with an audible beat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exponent' looks like a champion or advocate of the record, but it is the mathematical sense. The ending is spelt RITHM but said like rhythm.
explanation.definitionFit: A logarithm is the power to which a base number must be raised to give a value, which is exactly an exponent.

clue.text: Female getting wind after car abandoned outside?

definitions.text: Female getting wind after car abandoned outside?

indicators.note: abandoned can mean unrestrained and wild, so these letters are let loose into a new order

blocks.note: F is the abbreviation for female
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A woman hears about a car left dumped out in the street.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: the person who gets wind of a car left outside is the one who tickets it. A traffic warden is the British official who enforces parking rules.
explanation.definitionFit: Patrolling the streets and catching illegally parked vehicles is precisely the job of this parking enforcement officer.

clue.text: Robust defending judge, one revolutionary prophet

indicators.note: to defend something is to stand around it, so one word encloses the others
a revolution turns things round, so the assembled letters are read backwards

blocks.note: hale means healthy and strong
J is the abbreviation for judge
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A tough figure protecting a judge, a lone rebel visionary.
explanation.walkthrough: J and I go inside HALE to make HAJILE, which is then turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: Elijah is one of the major Old Testament prophets, taken up to heaven in a chariot of fire.

clue.text: Not a day patient’s bag?

blocks.note: surface reading: a hospital patient who is staying in rather than going home the same day
setter's reading: the small suitcase holding enough for one night away

explanation.walkthrough: A patient kept in hospital overnight could be called an overnight case; the phrase also names a small travelling bag.
explanation.definitionFit: A compact suitcase packed with essentials for a single night's stay is the luggage meant, and it is the kit such an in-patient brings.

clue.text: Ready for some tennis

blocks.note: first meaning: prepared, as in ready, steady, go
second meaning: a unit of play in a tennis match, made up of games

explanation.surface: Someone is all prepared for a game on court.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means prepared as an adjective, and as a noun it is a group of games forming part of a tennis match.

clue.text: Instructed in pronunciation of tense

indicators.note: pronunciation is about how a word is said, so a word that sounds the same is wanted

blocks.note: tense meaning stretched tight

explanation.surface: A language teacher coaching pupils on saying the tenses of verbs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tense' looks grammatical, but it means stretched tight.
explanation.definitionFit: Taught is the past tense of teach, and to instruct someone is to teach them.

clue.text: Periodical by graduate is hot stuff!

blocks.note: mag is short for magazine
an MA, Master of Arts, is a graduate

explanation.surface: A magazine written by a graduate is a sensation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hot stuff' sounds like praise for an exciting article but is meant literally.
explanation.definitionFit: Magma is the molten rock beneath the earth's crust, extremely high in temperature, so it is literally scorching material.

clue.text: Reluctance to move one near it, somehow

indicators.note: somehow says the letters come together in some unstated way, so they must be rearranged

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is unwilling to shift a person close to something.
explanation.definitionFit: Inertia is the tendency of a body, or a person, to stay at rest and resist being set in motion.

clue.text: Row initially about cuts as an alternative

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word beside it
something that cuts into a word goes inside it, splitting it in two

blocks.note: the first letter of about
or introduces an alternative

explanation.surface: A quarrel starts over cutting something as another option.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' looks as if it belongs to Row, but it works on the following word; Row is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An oar is the pole with a blade used to row a boat, so the verb and its tool are linked by metonymy.

clue.text: Female relative invading pitch is showing off

indicators.note: an invader goes into territory, so one word enters the other

blocks.note: an aunt is a female relative
to pitch something is to throw or fling it

explanation.surface: An aunt running onto the football field is making an exhibition of herself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pitch' suggests a sports field, but it is the verb to throw.
explanation.definitionFit: Flaunting means displaying something ostentatiously, which is what showing off is.

clue.text: Locals embracing girl are natives of state

indicators.note: to embrace is to put your arms around, so one word wraps around another

blocks.note: a girl's name
a local is British slang for one's neighbourhood pub

explanation.surface: Residents hugging a young woman are all born in the same place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Locals' looks like residents, but in Britain your local is your nearest pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Indianans are people from Indiana, one of the American states, so they are its natives.

clue.text: Through which spirit is poured out of sight

definitions.text: Through which spirit is poured out
definitions.note: a noun phrase for a device

blocks.clueFragment: Through which spirit is poured out
blocks.note: first meaning: the measuring device fitted to an upturned spirits bottle in a British bar
second meaning: an adjective meaning relating to the eye or vision

explanation.surface: Something is poured away where nobody can see it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of sight' reads as one phrase, but the break comes after 'out'. An Optic is a British bar device dispensing a measured shot.
explanation.definitionFit: The trademark name covers the dispensing gadget on a spirits bottle, and as an adjective it means concerning eyes and vision.

clue.text: Killer at sea concealed bloomer

blocks.note: the orca or orc is the killer whale
hid is the past tense of hide

explanation.surface: A murderer on a ship hid his blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' suggests a gaffe, but it means something that blooms.
explanation.definitionFit: An orchid is a flowering plant, and anything that produces flowers can playfully be called a bloomer.

clue.text: Character waited for leave period

blocks.note: to go is to leave
a period is a full stop, or dot

explanation.surface: Someone awaited a figure during a spell of leave.
explanation.definitionFit: In Beckett's play Waiting for Godot the two tramps wait for this figure, who never arrives on stage.

clue.text: Bend in centre of field: ogle girls

indicators.note: the centre of a stretch of words holds the letters wanted, buried inside them

blocks.note: the letters run from the end of field, through ogle, into the start of girls

explanation.surface: A lad in the middle of a field stares at the girls.
explanation.walkthrough: A dogleg is a sharp bend, especially a golf hole that turns partway along the fairway.
explanation.definitionFit: A dogleg is a sharp angle or kink in a road or golf hole, shaped like a dog's hind leg.

clue.text: Call concerning result?

definitions.note: verb sense: to result is to come about as a consequence

blocks.note: to call on someone is to come and visit
about means on the subject of

explanation.surface: A phone call asking about the outcome of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'result' looks like a noun but is the verb, as in what results; the question mark marks the loose fit.
explanation.definitionFit: To come about means to happen or arise, and something that results from a cause arises from it.

clue.text: Triumphant expression every second from rash lad

indicators.note: every second asks for the letters in even positions, skipping each one before

blocks.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters of rash lad

explanation.surface: A reckless boy's cry of victory, made instantly.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation is uttered in triumph or satisfaction at discovering or catching something out.

clue.text: Each leading

blocks.note: first meaning, read as two words: per person, as in ten pounds a head
second meaning: in front, in the lead

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense splits the answer into two words, A HEAD, which is how a price per person is put.
explanation.definitionFit: Split in two it means per person, like each; joined up it is an adverb meaning in front of the others.

clue.text: Find lie’s upset non-believer

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disordered, so the letters are thrown into a new arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An unbeliever is distressed to discover a falsehood.
explanation.definitionFit: An infidel is someone who does not believe in a given religion, so a disbeliever or unbeliever.

clue.text: Pro might, abandoning civil engineer

indicators.note: abandoning something means leaving it behind, so those letters are dropped

blocks.note: might is strength or power
the standard abbreviation of this professional title

explanation.surface: A professional may quit a job in civil engineering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pro' looks like a professional, but it means in favour of.
explanation.definitionFit: Being pro something means being in favour of it, the same as being for it.

clue.text: Knowing a king is held in great respect

indicators.note: something held in something else sits inside it, so one letter goes within the other word

blocks.note: taken as written
R is short for rex, Latin for king
awe is reverential respect

explanation.surface: Being conscious that a monarch is revered.
explanation.definitionFit: To be aware is to have knowledge or consciousness of something, so knowing is a direct adjectival synonym.

clue.text: Different strangers Des offended

indicators.note: making something different changes its form, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, a man's name

explanation.surface: Unfamiliar people upset a man called Des.
explanation.walkthrough: 'offended' looks like it means upset someone, but here it means did wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: To offend in the old sense is to break a law or commit a sin, which is to transgress.
